investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps required by the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining VM slots (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also unavailable — no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 132–144 seconds across all three sibling checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and a full contract-gap failure. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource pool fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run: all three sibling checks received the identical Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm message, indicating zero remaining VM slots across both peerpods-capable nodes.

Secondary — node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to the 2 peerpods nodes, leaving no fallback nodes even if VM capacity were available on other nodes; the 4 non-matching nodes cannot be used regardless of their general resource availability.

Tertiary — no preemption victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes, meaning no lower-priority pods can be evicted to free VM slots; the cluster has no automatic scale-out path visible to the scheduler at the time of the run.

Lower confidence — a transient spike in concurrent remote-agent provisioning requests (from other users or automated jobs) may have consumed all VM slots immediately before the eval run, rather than a sustained capacity shortfall; this cannot be confirmed without cluster metrics.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place new pods: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1905 never completed, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written, causing the expected-output contract to fail entirely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every new remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner cannot create a remote agent, so it never reaches the state-polling step and produces no evidence. This is an eval-layer signal of a real infrastructure constraint; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet to confirm a broader production outage.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhausted on both eligible nodes — all 3 remote-agent checks carry the identical scheduler error, indicating the resource pool was fully consumed before or during the eval run.

SECONDARY: Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes — only 2 nodes are configured to run kata peer-pod workloads; if those 2 are saturated there is no fallback capacity, making the cluster effectively zero-capacity for new remote-agent pods.

TERTIARY: Preemption disabled or ineffective for kata.peerpods.io/vm — the scheduler message 'No preemption victims found' and 'Preemption is not helpful for scheduling' indicates existing pods on the 2 eligible nodes cannot be evicted to free the resource, possibly due to PodDisruptionBudgets, priority classes, or the resource being non-preemptible.

The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs:1903) is intended to handle this, but if a previous run crashed before cleanup it could leave stale pods.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps required by the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining VM slots (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also unavailable — no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 132–144 seconds across all three sibling checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and a full contract-gap failure. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource pool fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run: all three sibling checks received the identical Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm message, indicating zero remaining VM slots across both peerpods-capable nodes.

Secondary — node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to the 2 peerpods nodes, leaving no fallback nodes even if VM capacity were available on other nodes; the 4 non-matching nodes cannot be used regardless of their general resource availability.

Tertiary — no preemption victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes, meaning no lower-priority pods can be evicted to free VM slots; the cluster has no automatic scale-out path visible to the scheduler at the time of the run.

Lower confidence — a transient spike in concurrent remote-agent provisioning requests (from other users or automated jobs) may have consumed all VM slots immediately before the eval run, rather than a sustained capacity shortfall; this cannot be confirmed without cluster metrics.

Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1905 never completed, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written, causing the expected-output contract to fail entirely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every new remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner cannot create a remote agent, so it never reaches the state-polling step and produces no evidence. This is an eval-layer signal of a real infrastructure constraint; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet to confirm a broader production outage.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in sequence on 2026-07-01 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes had only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, no remote agent VM was ever provisioned, and the eval runner never received any response evidence — leaving all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 eligible peer-pod nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state) confirms that no scheduling path exists under current cluster state. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no evidence of user-traffic or incident signals is present in the packet, so this is an eval-level failure only.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod\'s node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was stuck unscheduled for 144s before the check timed out.

sibling.remote-agent-create: identical scheduling failure ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn\'t match Pod\'s node affinity/selector') reported 132s into the earlier create check, ending at 2026-07-01T10:17:09.302Z.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduling failure reported 142s into the state check, ending at 2026-07-01T10:19:38.452Z — the three failures span a continuous ~5-minute window, consistent with sustained resource exhaustion rather than a transient blip.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — the eval runner received no response payload at all, confirming the agent VM was never started.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing, consistent with the probe never reaching the agent runtime.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=149711 — the check ran for ~150s, well past the 132–144s unschedulable window, confirming the timeout was driven by the scheduling stall.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918, which must provision a remote VM pod — this is the call that triggers the scheduling request that fails.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 peer-pod-capable nodes: existing remote agent VMs or other peer-pod workloads are consuming all available VM slots, leaving none for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are at capacity, no fallback exists.

Tertiary — a prior eval run's cleanup may have failed, leaving orphaned peer-pod VMs that are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots. The runner uses withCleanup (source-context run-status-probes.mjs:1916) but a cleanup failure from a previous run could leave resources stranded.

affectedAreas.label: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool (production-api cluster)
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on both peer-pod-capable nodes (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state). This is the immediate blocking constraint.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature — all three eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature (lines 183–185 of features.json) failed with the same scheduling error within a 5-minute window, indicating the entire remote-agent provisioning path is blocked.

affectedAreas.label: Remote agent VM provisioning path in eval runner
affectedAreas.reason: The runner calls createAgent with type 'remote' at line 1918, which triggers the peer-pod scheduling request. The scheduling failure prevents any agent from being created, so no evidence is ever collected.

affectedAreas.label: Node affinity/selector configuration for remote-agent pods
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by node affinity/selector (failed-check.message), concentrating all scheduling pressure onto 2 nodes. The affinity configuration is implicated but the exact pod spec or node label is not present in the supplied evidence.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm slot utilization on the 2 peer-pod nodes to determine whether exhaustion is ongoing or has cleared.
Audit all running peer-pod pods for orphaned eval VMs that may have survived a failed withCleanup call in a prior probe run; terminate any that are no longer needed.
If slots are genuinely exhausted by legitimate workloads, evaluate scaling the peer-pod node pool or increasing the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit on existing nodes.
Review the node affinity/selector configuration for remote-agent pods to confirm that restricting scheduling to 2 nodes is intentional and that the pool size is sufficient for concurrent eval runs.

Once cluster capacity is restored, re-run all three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) together to confirm the full provisioning and runtime path is healthy.

Consider adding a pre-flight capacity check to the eval runner that verifies kata.peerpods.io/vm availability before attempting agent creation, so future failures surface a clearer diagnostic message rather than a scheduling timeout.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies which workloads are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and whether any are orphaned eval pods from a prior withCleanup failure.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the scheduling failure is still active or has self-resolved, and produces fresh evidence for the contract gap (missing orgId, agentId, model, provider, message).

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Check node labels on all 6 nodes to verify affinity/selector scope
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms which nodes carry the label required by the remote-agent pod affinity, verifying that only 2 nodes are eligible and that the selector configuration is intentional.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect pending or recently failed remote-agent pod events
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Provides the exact scheduler rejection events and timestamps, confirming the duration and recurrence of the unschedulable condition.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm slots available and unused on the peer-pod nodes at the time of the failure, resource exhaustion would be disproved and a different cause (e.g., a broken pod spec, missing node label, or API-level rejection) would need to be investigated.
If re-running the eval immediately after this failure succeeded without any cluster changes, it would suggest a transient scheduling race rather than sustained exhaustion.

If the 4 non-peer-pod nodes were shown to have been incorrectly labeled or had their affinity rules changed around the time of the failure, the root cause would shift from capacity exhaustion to a misconfiguration of node selectors.

If orphaned peer-pod VMs from a previous eval run were found and cleaned up, and the eval then passed, it would confirm cleanup failure as the proximate cause of exhaustion rather than organic workload pressure.

If the local-agent-runtime or local-agent-create sibling checks (which do not use kata.peerpods.io/vm) were also failing at the same time, it would suggest a broader API or authentication failure rather than a peer-pod-specific capacity issue.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated counts on peer-pod nodes and fails with a capacity warning before any agent creation is attempted.
Add a cleanup-verification eval that lists peer-pod pods after each remote-agent probe run and asserts that no eval-created pods remain, catching withCleanup failures before they exhaust the VM pool.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that asserts the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., >= 2 with at least N free VM slots), alerting on pool shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.
